subject: Renewal planning + mid-cycle capacity bump — pricing options & procurement timing
messages:
From: Emma Zhao <emma@nebula-labs.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Paul Chen <paul.chen@nebula-labs.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning + quick ask re: mid-cycle top-up

Hey Ben —

Quick context: we hit a higher-than-expected usage spike in Aug and are forecasting a sustained 2.5-3x increase for the next 6–9 months. Our renewal with Redwood is in mid-February 2027.

Two asks:
- Can you provide a firm price / example structure for a mid-cycle capacity top-up that we could either (a) buy as a one-off add-on, or (b) annualize and co-term to Feb 2027?
- Any guidance on typical discount bands for annualizing mid-contract uplift (we're comfortable with committing to a higher run-rate if the economics work).

We also need procurement timing: our finance team needs an estimate for PO and approver timeline this quarter. I attached the updated SOW with projected usage.

Appreciate a quick outline so we can brief procurement.

—Emma
Emma Zhao
Head of Platform Engineering, Nebula Labs
emma@nebula-labs.com
Attachments: Nebula_SOW_v1.docx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Zhao <emma@nebula-labs.com>
Cc: Paul Chen <paul.chen@nebula-labs.com>
Date: Fri, 25 Sep 2026 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning + quick ask re: mid-cycle top-up

Emma — thanks for the note and the SOW. Congrats on the product momentum — understandable spike. Below are three pragmatic paths we've seen work for customers in this situation. I'll run numbers with our pricing ops and follow up with a formal proposal by end of next week.

High-level options (estimates):

1) One-time top-up (fastest)
- Purchase incremental capacity at list rates; optional prepay credit (5% off) for immediate invoicing
- Minimal contracting (amendment), procurement 3–10 business days

2) Annualize and co-term (best unit economics)
- Convert the uplift to an annualized commit for remaining term (example: convert 9 months of uplift -> annual equivalent), apply tiered discount based on committed annual units (range we typically offer: 8–15% depending on band/volume)
- Requires amendment + billing schedule; procurement ~10–20 business days depending on PO processing and legal review

3) Hybrid burst credits + reserved buffer
- Keep base renewal as-is, add reserved burst credits with a smaller committed top-up (lower discount) and short-term overage pricing

Questions for you to help me size the formal proposal:
- Target annualized run-rate you are willing to commit to (ballpark)
- Preferred invoice cadence (monthly vs quarterly vs upfront)
- Any internal approval deadlines for the quarter?

I'll loop in our sales ops to lock bands and get a proposal over. Would you be available for a 30-min call Monday to finalize assumptions?

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 26 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Nebula Labs — mid-cycle uplift -> pricing bands + approval request

Marissa / Lauren — looping you in for quick approval on discount bands and guidance on invoice cadence. Emma at Nebula sent updated SOW (attached in thread). They want options for a one-off top-up vs annualizing to co-term (renewal Feb 15, 2027).

Key facts:
- Estimated uplift: ~3x baseline for next 6–9 months; they signaled readiness to annualize if we can get to ~600k units/year (rough)
- Renewal: Feb 15, 2027 (about 5 months away)
- Procurement: CFO wants a PO estimate by Oct 8 to slot into Q4 processing

My suggested bands for approval (for proposal doc):
- Band A: 0–250k annualized units -> 6% discount (fast-approve)
- Band B: 250k–600k -> 12% discount
- Band C: 600k+ -> 18% discount (requires Rev Ops sign-off for deeper discount)

Invoice cadence options: monthly invoice (higher flexibility), quarterly billed/annualized (preferred for them?) or 50% upfront + monthly balance. We should include a 30-day PO acceptance window and a 20-business-day expected legal turnaround in the proposal.

Can you confirm: 1) approve Band B at 12% for this deal and 2) confirm whether Band C needs a specific margin floor or an approval slack? If approved, I will finalize numbers and send a PDF proposal + DocuSign link to Emma.

Thanks — Ben

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Zhao <emma@nebula-labs.com>
Cc: Paul Chen <paul.chen@nebula-labs.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2026 17:06:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Nebula mid-cycle uplift — two options (proposal attached)

Emma — thanks for the call earlier this week. Per our conversation, attached is a concise proposal and two paths you can take. I pulled conservative unit definitions so procurement has a clean PO amount to review.

Option 1 — One-time top-up (rapid execution)
- Deliverable: 75k additional units/month for 6 months (one-off top-up)
- Price: list price for units; 5% prepay credit if paid upfront
- Contract: simple amendment, estimated procurement 5–10 business days

Option 2 — Annualize & co-term (recommended for cost savings)
- Deliverable: Annualized commit equivalent = 600k units/year (reflects uplift scaled over remaining contract)
- Discount: 12% applied to annualized units (Band B)
- Billing: invoice quarterly in arrears (can change to monthly on request); 30-day payment terms
- Contract: amendment + side letter; estimated procurement + legal 10–20 business days

Other notes:
- We can include a small safety buffer (5% reserved burst credits) for usage variability; those credits are billed only if consumed.
- If Nebula can commit to Band C thresholds (700k+), we can revisit deeper discounting — will require Rev Ops sign-off and an exec approval path.

Attached: Nebula_Redwood_Uplift_Proposal_v2.pdf (proposal with line-item numbers and invoice examples)
DocuSign: https://na1.docusign.net/envelope/ABC123456789
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/45871/company/nebula-labs (deal: DEAL-45871)

Next steps:
- Please confirm preferred option by Oct 8 so we can align PO timeline.
- If Option 2, share preferred invoice cadence and the name of the person who will sign the amendment (legal contact).

Happy to hop back on a 20-min call if you want the line-by-line numbers.

Best regards,
